cases.title: Morning Rush, Line 3
cases.presentation: A commuter train car fills with a faint vapor. On the platform: a woman with pinpoint pupils and runny nose only; a man drooling, wheezing, vomiting; and a teen seizing and cyanotic. All have been disrobed and decontaminated.
cases.question: Best antidote plan?
options: A: Atropine only for the teen.
D: Woman: observe (± 1 kit if symptoms progress); man: 1 kit, repeat atropine to dry secretions; teen: 3 kits + benzodiazepine + ventilation.
cases.explanation: Dose by severity. Vapor-only mild miosis/rhinorrhea may need no injector; moderate → 1 kit; severe → 3 kits + benzo and airway support. Titrate repeat atropine to secretions.

cases.title: Pulled From the Apartment
cases.presentation: Firefighters carry a 40-year-old man out of a smoky apartment fire (burning furniture/foam). He is unresponsive, BP 78/40, RR 6, SpO2 98% on the monitor.
cases.question: What's going on and what do you give?
options: D: Combined CO and cyanide toxicity — 100% O2/ventilation and hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV.
cases.explanation: Pulse oximetry can be falsely reassuring with CO. Shock and coma in a smoke victim = cyanide until proven otherwise. Hydroxocobalamin doesn't cause methemoglobinemia — safe with CO.

cases.title: The Hay Smell
cases.presentation: After a chemical plant leak, 12 workers mildly cough and say they smelled 'freshly mown hay'. All have normal vitals and want to go home.
cases.question: Disposition?
options: A: Treat as phosgene exposure: rest, O2 as needed, transport/observe ~24 h for delayed pulmonary edema.
cases.explanation: Phosgene's latent period fools everyone. Exertion accelerates the pulmonary edema — they should not walk out, drive home, or exercise.
cases.clinicalPearl: Hay smell today = wet lungs tonight.
